sections.skill: Find the only candidate left after every clue

questions.prompt: Which month is it? Its name has fewer than 8 letters. Its name contains the letter R. It is the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th or 11th month. Its name does not start with J.
Which day of the week is it? Its name has no letter E. It comes after Wednesday in the week that starts on Monday. Its name has exactly 6 letters. Its name contains the letter U.
A whole number from 1 to 50 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7. It is greater than 20. It is even. It does not leave remainder 4 when divided by 5. What is the number?
Three friends, Ana, Ben and Cai, each have exactly one pet: a cat, a dog or a fish, all different. Ana does not have the dog. Ben has neither the cat nor the dog. Which pet does each friend have?
questions.correct_answer: Ana: cat; Ben: fish; Cai: dog

questions.prompt: A locker number is one of 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27. It is even. It is not a multiple of 4. Which locker is it?

sections.skill: Strategy: cross out, one clue at a time
sections.relationship: Students who guess usually try to hold all clues in mind. Writing the full candidate list and crossing out what each clue rules out makes the elimination complete and checkable.
sections.author_note: Students who guess usually try to hold all clues in mind. Writing the full candidate list and crossing out what each clue rules out makes the elimination complete and checkable.

lesson.title: Cross out, one clue at a time
text: Write down every candidate first: all 12 months, all 7 days, every number in range.
Apply ONE clue at a time and cross out every candidate it rules out. Do not skip a candidate because it "seems" unlikely.
When the clues are done, exactly one candidate should be left. If more than one is left, the clues are not enough; if none is left, recheck the work.

example.title: Worked example (a different list)
prompt: A number from 1 to 20: it is a multiple of 3; it is odd; it is greater than 10.
steps: Exactly one is left, so the number is 15.

questions.prompt: A number from 1 to 10 is even, greater than 7 and less than 10. What is it?
A day of the week (Monday to Sunday) starts with T and has more than 7 letters. Which day?
How many months have a name with exactly 4 letters?
If two candidates are left after every clue, the clues determine the answer.
Candidates: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Clue 1: the number is prime. Clue 2: the number is odd. How many candidates are left?

sections.skill: Eliminate with clues about neighbors and positions
sections.relationship: Harder: clues about the month before or after, and two-way clues.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: Which month is it? The month before it has a name longer than 5 letters. The month after it does not end in "ber". The month after it contains the letter U. Its own name contains the letter A.
In the week Monday to Sunday, exactly one day has a name whose day before and day after both contain the letter T.
A whole number from 1 to 100 is a perfect square, is odd, has two digits, and its digits add to 13. What is it?
Four runners, Dev, Eva, Finn and Gia, finished 1st to 4th, no ties. Eva finished right after Dev. Gia finished before Finn. Finn finished before Dev. Assign each runner a place.
Candidates are the whole numbers 1 to 30. Clues: A: the number is odd. B: it is a multiple of 3. C: it is greater than 10. D: it is a multiple of 5. Which number fits all four clues?

sections.relationship: Expert: find unnecessary clues and the least information that still determines the answer.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: Candidates are the whole numbers 1 to 30, with four clues: A: odd; B: a multiple of 3; C: greater than 10; D: a multiple of 5. Only 15 fits all four. Which ONE clue can be removed so that exactly one number is still left?
A number from 1 to 30 is a multiple of 4. What is the least number of extra yes/no questions of the form "Is it greater than k?" that always identify it?
Adding a new clue to a puzzle can never increase the number of candidates left.
Candidates are the whole numbers 1 to 20. Write a number n that survives BOTH clues: n is prime, and n leaves remainder 1 when divided by 4.
questions.rule: isPrime(n) and n % 4 == 1 and n >= 1 and n <= 20
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isPrime(n) and n % 4 == 1 and n >= 1 and n <= 20 (example: n = 5)

questions.prompt: Six boxes are numbered 1 to 6. One holds a prize. Which single clue, added alone, would leave exactly one box?

choices.text: "The box number is a multiple of 3."
"The box number is prime and even."

questions.correct_answer: "The box number is prime and even."
